questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: i liked the courses of the University and the buildings/campus which is very pretty.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The visiting student office was very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The visiting student office send mails with info and was very available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky. I made a facebook post in a local group and and a week later a lady reached out to me offering a room to rent. I can recommend facebook and all the flat share groups there!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is less sociable, but more local. I liked living with local roomies instead of only speaking to other exchange students, but I kind of missed out on all the social events happening on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled in a formula with the courses that I wanted and send it to the visiting student office. I then got an email back telling me what courses I was accepted in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The visiting student office was available all week

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful. I only got into one of my priorities and then had to reapply in another round because a lot of courses in my domain were full (local students have 1. priority)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be on time when applying! first come, first served. And make sure to list many courses because it is rare to get into your top choices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two on BA level and one courses with students from MA and BA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more traditional and less dialog based in two of the courses (at School of Divinity) that I had - a big lecture hall with many students and a professor speaking. But in one of my courses (at the Collage of Art) it was very close to what I have experienced at UCPH - a small class room with dialog and exchange.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Adam, Eve and LGBT+: Sex and Gender in The Hebrew Bible 
Apocalypse: The Book of Revelation in History and Culture 
Visions of the Buddha: Religious Art in Medieval Japan

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! they were so interesting and niche! something that I have not been able to find at UCPH and even though they were not my nr. 1 priority, I was so positively surprised.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I did not expect to spend so much on food, but I ate out a lot and went to many pubs which costs a lot! 
Also, I travelled a little around the country (in the highlands and to London) which made me spend more money than expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food! it is very expensive because of Brexit and the inflation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs were available, but they seemed a little closed off and more accesable for local students. Because I only stayed one semester (which passes so quickly) I did not even have the time to engage in the clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None, cause I did not participate in any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands! Visit all the museums (they are free). Go partying in Glasgow (they have a better night life). Take a walk at Arthur Seat or Blackford hill (less touristed). There are so many things to do in Edinburgh, but it would be too long to list them all - Look out for what the visiting student office plans and be sure to be a member of the exchange facebook groups were events are proposed

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It was honestly not a big culture chock from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: make friends with your class mates - it is easy because you already have something in common being in the same class. Some departments have ALG (Alternative learning groups) which makes it easy to get to know a group of people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is very nice and welcoming. Small talk is very accepted and people compliment each other way more

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Enjoy the courses without thinking about doing it perfect (the grades will not be transferred anyway). See it as a chance to make some mistakes and be guided by your interest
2) time passes so fast so make a rough schedule for the semester and make sure to plan all the thing you want to do before it is too late
3) download dating apps to meet local people! It is fun and a good way to get to know some locals

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to check the exam form before choosing a course! I didn't and ended up doing an exam where I had two write three essays in two hours on paper with a pen! it was very traditional and not at all something that I am used to.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get away from Copenhagen puts things in perspective and I think that I am more eager to go back now and learn more with new inputs.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: feeling a little lonely and getting FOMO when seeing what my friends were doing back home. and the exams! they are way more stressful and traditional.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
